sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **IAU 2006 Definition**: According to the International Astronomical Union (IAU), a planet must: (1) Orbit the Sun, (2) Have sufficient mass for its self-gravity to overcome rigid body forces so that it assumes a hydrostatic equilibrium (nearly round) shape, and (3) Have cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit.
• **Dwarf Planets**: Bodies that meet criteria (1) and (2) but have not cleared their neighbourhood and are not satellites (e.g., Pluto, Eris, Haumea, Makemake, Ceres).
• **Exoplanets (Extrasolar Planets)**: Planets orbiting stars outside our solar system, detected via transit method, radial velocity, direct imaging, and gravitational microlensing.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Hill Sphere radius defines the gravitational sphere of influence of a planet against perturbations from perturbing bodies.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Inner Solar System**: Dominated by high-density silicate rocks and iron cores.
• **Asteroid Belt**: Located between Mars and Jupiter, acting as a vestigial planetesimal zone prevented from forming a planet due to Jupiter's gravitational resonance.
• **Kuiper Belt & Oort Cloud**: Trans-Neptunian regions housing icy planetesimals and long-period comet reservoirs.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Space debris around Earth orbits, orbital congestion, planetary protection protocols for Mars/Moon missions.
• **Policy Interventions**: UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space (COPUOS), ISRO's interplanetary roadmap (Mangalyaan-2, Shukrayaan).

items.title: Mnemonic for Planetary Order from the Sun
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles'.
• **Decoded Meaning**: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly verifies sequence questions or spacing of inner vs outer planets.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember that Pluto was reclassified in 2006 because it failed the third IAU criterion (clearing its orbit), sharing its orbital zone with numerous Kuiper Belt Objects (KBOs).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often traps candidates by stating that dwarf planets are not part of the solar system or are classified as asteroids. Remember that dwarf planets are a distinct official IAU category, and Ceres is both an asteroid (largest in the belt) and a dwarf planet.
Mains Value Addition: Emphasize the significance of astrobiology and planetary habitability indices when answering questions on space exploration and ISRO's scientific missions.

keyTakeaways: Planets must satisfy three strict IAU criteria: orbit the Sun, attain hydrostatic equilibrium (round shape), and clear their orbital neighborhood.
The solar system is sharply divided by the frost line into rocky terrestrial inner planets and gaseous/icy outer Jovian planets.
Modern astronomy increasingly focuses on exoplanet discovery and atmospheric spectroscopy to search for biosignatures.
